description: Role model, authorization predicates, and the full permission matrix. READ THIS BEFORE ANY AUTH WORK. The role system is the most fragile subsystem in the codebase.

storage_format.warning: There is no normalisation, no CHECK constraint, and no roles table.

active_role.definition: session['role'] = available_roles[0] at login, or the value chosen via /switch_role
active_role.significance: CSV ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING. available_roles[0] decides the landing page and the monkeypatched value.
edge_cases: role='' yields session['role']=='' and routes to /dashboard

the_monkeypatch.what: Overrides psycopg.Cursor.fetchone globally so the CURRENT user's row has its role replaced by session['role'].
the_monkeypatch.why: Nearly every role check is exact string equality, which fails against CSV values. Rather than rewrite ~20 call sites, the app rewrites the row at read time.

semantics.scope: process-global; affects every psycopg.Cursor in the interpreter including secondary connections
semantics.trigger: fetchone() returning a dict containing BOTH 'role' and 'username' keys
semantics.restriction: only when row['username'] == session['username']; can never rewrite another user's row
semantics.requires: psycopg rows must be dict_row, else the patch is a silent no-op

limitations.consequence: Every list-shaped role decision is inconsistent with single-row ones. Concretely backend/app.py:2382 and the report dropdowns at backend/app.py:1856, 1860 show raw CSV while the gate used the patched role.

the_monkeypatch.do_not: Replacing this is a real refactor requiring a full audit of every role comparison plus a normalised role model. It is not a cleanup.

matching_strategies.reliability: only correct BECAUSE the monkeypatch replaced the CSV with one role

matching_strategies.code: split on comma, strip, lowercase, then test exact token membership
matching_strategies.reliability: handles CSV correctly and safely handles None/''
matching_strategies.caveat: 'IQAC Coordinator' (no qualifier) returns False, which is why the boot migration at backend/app.py:624 exists

matching_strategies.reliability: SUBSTRING MATCH on a CSV column. A role like 'Not A School IQAC Coordinator' would match. strpos(...)=0 is NOT the same as 'CSV does not contain this role'.

matching_strategies.code: LOWER(role)='admin' OR LOWER(role) LIKE '%secretary%' OR LOWER(designation) LIKE '%secretary%' OR LOWER(username) LIKE '%secretary%'
matching_strategies.reliability: very loose; also matches admins whose designation contains 'secretary'
WILL MISS most rows, because IN requires whole-string equality and multi-role CSV values like 'Secretary, Campus IQAC Coordinator' do not match.

global_guard.name: enforce_password_change
key_facts: It NEVER checks whether anyone is logged in. It only enforces the password-change flag. Every route implements its own login check separately.
The allowlist is keyed on request.endpoint (the function name), not the URL.
not request.endpoint short-circuits unmatched URLs, avoiding a redirect loop.
Being app-level, it DOES cover pdf.* blueprint endpoints.
home is NOT exempt, so a flagged user is redirected before home's own /login redirect runs.
It flashes on every intercepted request, so duplicate warnings accumulate.
It trusts the session flag, not the database. An admin password reset does not affect an already-open session.

session_keys.storage: signed client-side cookie; app.config is never assigned so Flask 3.0 defaults apply (HTTPONLY=True, SECURE=False, no SameSite)

keys.purpose: Identity key. Its presence IS the login test in every handler.
Display only; never re-validated against the DB
THE ACTIVE ROLE. Read by the monkeypatch.

logout_defect.problem: session.pop('username') only. role, full_name, available_roles, and must_change_password persist in the client cookie after logout.

authentication.csrf: NONE. No CSRF library in requirements.txt, no token on any form including /change_password.
authentication.custom_decorators: NONE. No @login_required or @admin_required anywhere. All 41 checks are hand-copied inline.

endpoint_grants.auth: COORD except pdf/report_standard_download which is SECRETARY-only

privilege_escalation_candidates.issue: Session-only check with no role check
privilege_escalation_candidates.impact: Any authenticated user can reach the endpoint

privilege_escalation_candidates.issue: Session check present but role check missing or admin-only
Routes with no authentication check at all

migration_guidance: Keep the Flask session cookie; switching to JWT requires reimplementing the monkeypatch semantics, before_request, and every inline guard.
Add GET /api/me returning the session dict verbatim; it is the only thing the Angular shell needs.
Replace /switch_role GET with POST /api/active-role, and add CSRF protection at the same time.
Mirror enforce_password_change as an Angular route guard, but treat it as convenience only; server checks stay authoritative.
Return 401 JSON for XHR instead of a 302, branching on X-Requested-With which sessionInterceptor already sends.
Do NOT trust client-side role gating; given substring matching and unpatched fetchall, client assumptions will diverge from the server view.
